title: Introduce location-bound service roles and audit token sanitizer
author: Priya Khatri
description:
Motivation: Customers operating across multiple legal jurisdictions asked for finer-grained enforcement so that service principals and machine roles can be constrained to a declared geography and service-residency policy. This PR introduces two cooperating features: (1) a location-bound service-role assertion adapter that augments RBAC v2 checks with geography-residency predicates and KMS usage allowlists, and (2) an audit-token sanitizer that strips/normalizes ephemeral tokens in logs while preserving provenance metadata required for compliance audits.

Scope and changes: Single PR touching authz, audit, config and docs. Key changes: updated RBAC v2 schema to accept optional "location_assertions" for service roles; new adapter component that evaluates request metadata (region, tenant_residency, model_zone) and maps them to enforcement predicates; KMS usage allowlist lookup integrated into the adapter so cryptographic operations are validated against configured region policies; audit-token sanitizer middleware that replaces raw bearer token fragments and wraps provenance into signed audit envelope headers; configuration authoring helper (pkg/config/region_policies.yaml) and console docs for operators.

Compatibility and rollout: Default behavior is opt-in (adapter disabled by default). Cluster operators can enable the adapter via the feature flag security.location_bound_roles=true in platform config. When enabled the adapter enforces additional checks but falls back to permissive mode for roles without a location_assertion field so existing role files keep working. KMS allowlist entries are additive; if absent, crypto calls are permitted unless strict_kms_policy=true is set.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for schema parsing, assertion evaluation and sanitizer token edge cases. Integration harness added a simulated cross-region call to validate reject/allow transitions and audit envelope generation. Local canary ran against perf-canary cluster; no measurable latency regression observed in slo-targeted percentile (p99 increased by <3ms in synthetic tests). CI includes static analysis, contract tests and end-to-end audit ingestion smoke.

Rollout plan: 1) merge gated behind feature-flag; 2) staged rollout to internal infra clusters for 48h with audit sampling enabled; 3) opt-in customers can enable via console; 4) after 2 weeks, flip strict_kms_policy to true for selected clusters and monitor regressions.

Related: complements ENG-6628 (data residency policy compiler) and SEC-88 (audit retention hardening). Linear tickets are listed above.
